absent: Locking, sleeping, interrupt, and preemption rules for mappings beyond the shown fault and preemption restores.
Persistent high memory window management, eviction, slot allocation, and TLB handling.
Page table, reverse mapping, and fault handling state machines for huge pages.
HMM range fault, notifier, snapshot, and DMA mapping lifecycle and error handling.
mTHP counter lifecycle, per-CPU concurrency, and THP collapse and split policies.
Cache maintenance requirements on aliasing architectures beyond the shown flush calls.
Folio and page structure layouts, flag definitions, and allocator behavior.
Sanitizer tag and metadata handling beyond the shown call sites.

findings.text: In the configuration shown, temporary kernel mapping of a page is a direct address translation without an extra window. Mapping may sleep and returns the direct address of the supplied page, reverse lookup converts a mapped address back through the direct map, unmapping only performs an optional architecture flush, and the flush-unused helper does nothing.

Local and atomic mapping variants in this configuration also resolve directly. Local mapping of a page, of a folio at a byte offset, of a frame number, and the panic-tolerant and protection-ignored forms all return direct addresses. Local unmap optionally flushes the containing page. Atomic unmap additionally re-enables page faults and then restores migration on realtime builds or preemption otherwise.

Unmap entry macros guard against passing a page structure where an address is expected by failing the build in that case, then delegate to the corresponding internal unmap routine inside a single-statement wrapper.

High memory accounting has two shapes. One delegates free and total counts to internal counters and treats an address as a temporary mapping when it falls in the persistent mapping window or in the fixed mapping window for temporary slots. The other reports both counts as zero and never classifies an address as a temporary mapping.

Several cache and virtual range helpers are inert in the shown fragments. Anonymous page flush, kernel virtual range flush and invalidate, huge pud accessed marking, and memory failure queueing accept their usual address and size or page and frame arguments and produce no effect.

User and kernel page clearing is layered. Single user page clearing delegates to the raw page clear, multi-page clearing either iterates per page or uses a contiguous clear optimization, high memory variants acquire a temporary local mapping around the clear and release it afterwards, the tagged variant clears through an untagged view, and a tag helper simply echoes its boolean input.

Allocation entry for a zeroed movable folio takes a virtual area and address, requests a single high-user movable folio, and when the allocation policy requires zeroing it clears the first page through the user high page path before returning the folio, propagating allocation failure as a null return.
User allocation needs explicit zeroing when either data or instruction caches can alias, or when initialization on allocation is not enabled by default, as tested through a static branch.

Range zeroing maps the target page locally, validates that both range ends lie within the page extent, zeroes each non-empty interval, releases the mapping, and flushes the data cache for every constituent page of a compound page. Single interval and folio based wrappers for one range, two ranges, and start plus length all delegate to the two interval form.

Page and folio extents derive from the base page size scaled by the compound or folio order. Compound page count is one unless the head flag is set, in which case it comes from the large folio count, which itself is either a stored count or one shifted by the large order. In-page and in-folio offsets are the low bits below the respective size.

Full page copies map both source and destination with local mappings, copy one page through a user cache aware primitive or a raw page copy with sanitizer handling, then release the destination mapping before the source mapping.

Tolerant copies have two shapes. One attempts a machine check tolerant kernel copy under local mappings, preserves sanitizer state on success, releases both mappings, and on residual failure queues a memory failure for the source frame before returning the residual. The other simply delegates to the plain copy and always reports success.

Page scoped move and set helpers validate that offset plus length stays within one page, operate through temporary local mappings of source and destination, and release the mappings afterwards. The write and zero forms additionally flush the destination data cache.

Folio scoped copies validate against the whole folio size and proceed in chunks that never cross a page boundary when the involved folio requires partial mapping. Each chunk is mapped, copied, and released with progress advanced until the request is complete. Writes flush the folio cache at the end, and the file positioned read clamps the length by the offset inside the folio or page.

Tail helpers start from a folio offset with an existing or fresh local mapping, step page by page while the remaining length exceeds the current page remainder under partial mapping, copy or zero each step, flush the folio cache, and return the current mapping so the caller can release it. The fill form copies the supplied bytes then zeroes the remainder through the zero tail path.

Reference release for folios first releases a caller supplied local mapping and then drops one folio reference. Dropping checks for a zero count transition and only then invokes the final free path, with a debug check that the count was not already zero.
The virtual memory debug check has two builds. One behaves as a fatal runtime check on its condition, the other only validates the expression at build time and produces no runtime code.
Device memory map for heterogeneous management holds an IOVA state object, a pointer to an array of frame numbers, a pointer to an array of DMA addresses, and the size of one DMA entry.

Heterogeneous range descriptor holds a notifier pointer, a sequence snapshot, a start and end virtual address, a pointer to an array of tagged frame entries, default flag bits, a mask selecting which flag bits matter, and an owner cookie for private device memory.

Tagged frame entries expose converters that strip flag and order bits to recover the frame number before translating to a page structure or physical address, plus an extractor that shifts down the order field and keeps its low five bits as the mapping order.

Encoding reserves upper bits of a word. HMM_PFN_VALID marks validity and also means fault request while HMM_PFN_WRITE marks writability and also means write request and HMM_PFN_ERROR marks error. Persistence across calls is provided by HMM_PFN_DMA_MAPPED plus HMM_PFN_P2PDMA and HMM_PFN_P2PDMA_BUS for peer paths. Order sits at HMM_PFN_ORDER_SHIFT as five bits and HMM_PFN_FLAGS masks all flag plus order bits.

THP_ORDERS_ALL_ANON covers anonymous orders above one through PMD. THP_ORDERS_ALL_SPECIAL_DAX covers PMD and PUD for special DAX while THP_ORDERS_ALL_FILE_DEFAULT covers file cache orders above zero, with THP_ORDERS_ALL as their union. HPAGE_PMD_SHIFT and HPAGE_PUD_SHIFT either alias page table shifts or fail the build. From each shift the corresponding order subtracts page shift, the count shifts one by order, the size shifts one by shift, and the mask clears low size bits for both PMD and PUD levels.

Transparent huge policy enumeration orders an unsupported marker first, then a general flag, a madvise request flag, several defrag selectors for direct, kswapd, combined, requested and khugepaged paths, and finally a zero page use flag. Validation context TVA_SMAPS means smaps exposure while TVA_PAGEFAULT means fault service and TVA_KHUGEPAGED plus TVA_FORCED_COLLAPSE mean background and forced collapse. Multi-size transparent huge statistics enumerate fault alloc and fallback, collapse alloc and failure and exceed reasons, swap and shared memory paths, split outcomes, and anonymous counts. Default heterogeneous range wait is 1000.
Multi-size transparent huge statistics table is a two dimensional array of counters indexed first by order up to the maximum order derived from entries per table and second by the statistic kind.

Statistic update either ignores nonpositive or above PMD orders and otherwise adds a delta to the per CPU table for the given order and item with a single increment wrapper, or does nothing in the disabled build. Allowable order testing checks whether the bit for an order appears in the allowed set for a virtual area, and folio splitting delegates to the list form with a null list.
Each shown header defines its include guard macro once to prevent multiple inclusion.

Callers must keep offsets and lengths inside the target page or folio because helpers only enforce this with debug checks that may be compiled out, and must not pass an already freed page since the put path asserts a nonzero count. Zeroing beyond the page extent is treated as a fatal programming error, and unmap macros reject page pointers at build time.
